tonight.headline: Nobody plays until Thursday. The week is decided at 01:00 tomorrow.
body: You are 0-2 and you draw Footballers, who are 2-0 with the second-most points in the league. ESPN projects you 127.65 to their 94.01, which is a 67% win probability and the softest matchup you have had. Do not trust the 94.01.

Their lineup projects that low because two starting slots currently read 0.0: Caleb Williams at quarterback and Dallas Goedert at tight end, both doubtful. They have no backup quarterback and Brock Bowers, their only other tight end, is out. They hold waiver priority 8. They will try to fix the quarterback slot tomorrow morning, and you sit at priority 2.

case.label: The thing you can actually do to them
case.body: Footballers need a quarterback and so do Bok-aneers and Nicky Jam — three of the ten teams in this league have no healthy passer. Bok-aneers' Jaxson Dart sprained his MCL on the opening drive against the Rams and SNY's Connor Hughes reports the team is bracing for a two-to-four week absence. Nicky Jam's Jayden Daniels dislocated his elbow and Dan Quinn said Monday he would 'rather defer and wait' on a timeline until specialists report back Thursday or Friday. Footballers' Caleb Williams is week-to-week with a hamstring per Ben Johnson. Brock Purdy, 90.2% rostered, sits on waivers clearing at 01:00 tomorrow.

case.label: Why their 94.01 is a lie in your favour anyway
case.body: Even after they claim a quarterback, the tight end hole stays. Goedert is doubtful with a knee, Bowers is out, and there is no third tight end on the roster. Their real ceiling this week is somewhere around 110-115, not 94 and not the 133 they averaged over two weeks. You project 127.65 before any of the three moves below.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Footballers landing Purdy or Bo Nix ahead of you — they claim from priority 8 and you from 2, so on a contested claim you win. If Goedert practises Wednesday and Thursday and is upgraded, their tight end slot goes from 0.0 to about 11 and this stops being a soft matchup.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Wednesday 01:00 your time · about twelve hours
doFirst.title: Claim Brock Purdy, drop Kyle Pitts
doFirst.subtitle: Three of ten teams have no quarterback, one of them is your opponent this week, and you claim from priority 2.

case.label: The league error
case.body: Bok-aneers, Footballers and Nicky Jam all carry exactly one quarterback and all three are hurt: Dart's MCL (two to four weeks per SNY), Caleb Williams' hamstring (week-to-week per Ben Johnson), Daniels' dislocated elbow (no timeline, specialists reporting Thursday or Friday). Purdy is 90.2% rostered nationally and unowned here. He is 2-0, 45 of 56 for 492 yards, five touchdowns and one interception, a 125.6 rating, and in Week 2 he went 20 of 22 for 287 against Miami. He is not a stash, he is the best quarterback on any wire in either of your leagues.

case.label: Why the claim is nearly free
case.body: Chem resets waiver order weekly. The runbook's own rule is that a speculative claim here costs nothing lasting, and you have moved from 10 of 10 to 2 of 10 because you are 0-2. The only cost is the roster seat and the drop. One caveat, stated plainly: a successful claim sends you to the back of the order for the rest of this waiver run, so you should expect to win one contested claim tomorrow, not two. If you want the certain points instead of the asset, fire the Lions card first and let this one go.

case.label: Why Pitts is the seat, against a 92.9% market
case.body: Dropping a player rostered in nine of ten leagues needs a reason on the record, so here it is. The quarterback argument everyone is using is dead — Michael Penix Jr. is confirmed as Atlanta's Week 3 starter, full participant with the knee, with Tua second and Cooper Rush third on the official Thursday depth chart. It does not matter. Pitts played 26 of 69 offensive snaps in Week 2, 38%, fewer than backup tight ends Charlie Woerner (33) and Austin Hooper (30), and turned it into one catch for 15 yards. He has 1 catch on 4 targets all season. In Chem the flex is RB/WR only, so a second tight end cannot enter your lineup under any circumstance. He is a bench seat that cannot pay.

case.label: What you do with Purdy after
case.body: He never starts for you — Josh Allen is the highest-projected quarterback in the league at 23.8 and is in a 50.5-point game. Purdy is trade inventory. Bok-aneers have Jahmyr Gibbs, Breece Hall and Cam Skattebo and no quarterback for the next month; that is the first conversation. I cannot price that trade for you today, because Purdy is not on your roster yet and this brief only proposes trades it has computed on both rosters. That is also why this is ELITE and not LEGENDARY: the claim is real, the payoff is a negotiation I have not been able to verify.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Guillo-tinas, who hold priority 1 and already carry Lamar Jackson and Patrick Mahomes, file on Purdy anyway as a block — they are the only team that outranks you and they have no need, so it would be pure denial. Or all three quarterback-poor teams settle for Bo Nix, Kyler Murray or Tyler Shough, which are all on the same wire, and nobody has to pay you anything for Purdy. In that case you drop him next week having spent one bench seat.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Wednesday 01:00 your time · about twelve hours
doFirst.title: Claim the Lions D/ST, drop the Ravens
doFirst.subtitle: Baltimore play the highest-total game on the entire Week 3 board. That is the worst place a defence can be.

case.label: The number that decides it
case.body: Ravens at Cowboys in Brazil carries a 52.5 over/under — the highest of all sixteen Week 3 games, against a board where the median is about 44. Baltimore are only 3-point favourites, so the implied Dallas total is roughly 24.75. Detroit host the Jets at -6.5 with a 47.5 total, which implies about 20.5 for New York. You are moving your defence out of the league's biggest shootout and into a game where the opponent is implied under 21.

case.label: The conflict, named rather than hidden
case.body: Garrett Wilson is your starting receiver and he is a Jet. Claiming the Lions means one of your two starting slots is betting against the other. That is a real cost and I am not going to pretend it is free — but Wilson's own usage is the argument for doing it anyway: 88% route participation and only a 21% target share, with Adonai Mitchell leading the Jets in Week 2 at 32%. If you would rather not hedge yourself, the Jaguars D/ST at 7.2 against New England is the clean alternative and still beats Baltimore's 6.0.

case.label: Why the Giants card from yesterday is withdrawn
case.body: Yesterday this brief told you to add the Giants D/ST on a Draft Sharks Week 3 ranking of 2nd. Jaxson Dart has since been ruled out with a sprained MCL and Jameis Winston starts. New York opened as 5.5-point home favourites and are now 3, with a 40.5 total. A defence whose own offence just lost its quarterback gets fewer leads to protect and fewer pass-rush situations. The ranking was built before the injury.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Detroit are without their pass rush by Sunday — no Week 3 injury report exists yet, the first is filed Wednesday. Or Baltimore's 52.5 collapses on Cowboys injury news, which Yardbarker trailed Monday as 'brutal injury updates' for the Dallas defence; a lower total would partly rehabilitate the Ravens. Note the same 52.5 is why Tyler Loop stays at kicker.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Sunday 11:00 your time · both games kick together
doFirst.title: Move Jalen Coker into the flex over Terry McLaurin
doFirst.subtitle: Third time this card has been written. It has never been executed, and the case is stronger than yesterday.

case.label: This was told to you yesterday and the day before
case.body: The activity log shows AVIATO has made no move since 16 September. McLaurin is still in the flex and Coker is still on your bench. Rosters are unlocked right now and this costs nothing — no claim, no priority, no drop. It is the single cheapest point-gain available to you and it has been sitting there for four days.

case.label: The environment, which is new today
case.body: Washington's implied team total against Seattle is 17.0 — the lowest of any team you own a player on, in a 40.5-point game where Seattle are 6.5-point favourites. Carolina's is 19.5. Neither is good, but the gap in role is not close.

case.label: The two roles, measured
case.body: Coker played 57 of 61 snaps in Week 1 (93%) and has 16 catches on 18 targets across two games, an 88.9% catch rate, with 2 touchdowns, on a new three-year $35M deal, catching from a Bryce Young who has 648 yards and 6 touchdowns in two weeks. McLaurin has a 27.8% target share with Mariota — the volume is genuinely there — but a 30.8% catch rate, the worst in the NFL among players with ten or more targets, and 2 catches on 9 targets at Dallas.

case.label: The honest argument against, since it exists
case.body: Dan Quinn said the playbook does not shrink for Mariota: 'what do you wanna feature with Marcus that you didn't with Jayden? No pullback or any of that space.' And McLaurin averaged 3.53 yards per route run with Mariota throwing last season. If you believe target share is the durable signal, McLaurin is the hold. I am siding with Coker because a 93% snap share and an 88.9% catch rate are the same signal with the efficiency attached, and because Washington's 17.0 implied total caps the whole thing.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Mariota finds McLaurin eight or more times against Seattle while Cleveland hold Coker under five targets. That reverses it and the flex goes back next week. Reversible, costs a lineup slot and nothing else.

whatWentWrong.title: Brian Thomas Jr. has been benched for four days for the wrong reason
whatWentWrong.lead: This brief kept clearing him on the grounds that Jakobi Meyers was not taking his targets. Meyers was never the threat. Parker Washington is.

case.label: The number I did not have until today
case.body: Thomas's route share is 74%. Meyers is at 88% and Parker Washington is at 90%. Washington ranks second in the entire NFL at a 38% target share and is drawing 134 air yards a game, half of Jacksonville's total. Thomas is the third receiver by route participation on his own team.

case.label: Why the old clause kept passing
case.body: The falsification condition written on 18 September was Meyers-based: if Meyers out-targets him, bench him. Meyers drew one target in Week 2, so the clause kept resolving in Thomas's favour and the row was carried forward as healthy. The clause was measuring the wrong player. That is my error, not a data problem, and it survived four runs.

case.label: What it did not cost
case.body: Nothing, by luck. He has been on your bench the whole time and the flex went to McLaurin and Coker instead. But he was being held as a rebound candidate on a thesis that was never true, and he is now a drop candidate rather than a hold.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Parker Washington's 38% target share regressing — it is the second-highest in the league and two games is a small sample. If Thomas's route share crosses 85% against New England he is back to being a real asset. Until then he ranks below Monangai as the next seat I would spend.

worthALook.name: Rashod Bateman
worthALook.lead: Still the best role story on this wire, and Wednesday is the first day all season you could actually win him.

case.body: 80% of Baltimore's snaps in Week 1. In Week 2 against New Orleans he went 7 catches on 9 targets for 88 yards and a 22-yard touchdown, with Zay Flowers out and Ja'Kobi Lane on IR. Lamar Jackson said of him that he 'is actually going to get a lot more targets, I believe.' And he is in the 52.5-point game, the highest total on the board.

case.label: What changed in your favour
case.body: Priority. Every previous run declined him partly because you claimed from 10 of 10 and would lose a contested claim on a 24% receiver. You are 2 of 10 this week. The reason he is still a row rather than a card is not the claim any more — it is that Purdy and the Lions defence are worth more, and you realistically win one contested claim tomorrow.

case.label: The condition that has gone live
case.body: Jesse Minter said Monday that Flowers has a 'good shot' to play against Dallas 'as long as he makes progress in practice this week.' Flowers went 5 for 150 and a touchdown in the first half of Week 1 before the hamstring. If he returns, Bateman's nine-target week was an absence, not a role. The first real signal is Wednesday's practice report — which lands after waivers process.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Flowers being limited or out again on Wednesday's report turns this into a card next week. Flowers full-participant makes it a pass. If you would rather have the stash than Purdy, file this instead of that — not in addition to it.

worthALook.name: Adonai Mitchell
worthALook.lead: He out-targeted Garrett Wilson on your own starter's team last week and 83% of this league has not noticed.

case.label: The observation
case.body: In Week 2 Mitchell led the Jets with a 32% target share and a 28% target-per-route-run rate, ahead of Garrett Wilson's 21% and 16% on similar route volume. That is the shape the runbook calls a player whose number has not caught up to his role: he projects 10.7 and is rostered in one league in six.

case.label: Why it is a row and not a card
case.body: One week. Wilson still has an 88% route participation and a 2.13 yards-per-route-run career-high pace, and the Jets are implied at 20.5 against Detroit, so this is a small pie either way. Buying the second receiver on a low-total offence is not worth a claim you can only win once.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Mitchell clearing a 25% target share again at Detroit. Two weeks makes it a role rather than a game script, and at that point he is the claim and Brian Thomas Jr. is the drop.

doNotChase.name: Khalil Shakir
doNotChase.lead: This row has been carried for five runs waiting for a seat to open. I should have closed it on usage, and I am closing it now.

case.label: The number that ends it
case.body: Week 2 at Detroit: 50.4% snap share, 60% route share, 21.4% target share. He played 36 of 74 offensive snaps. Keon Coleman led all Bills receivers at 55, and SI's snap-count piece notes that three tight ends had more snaps than Buffalo's second-most-used receiver. A 60% route share is low-end WR2 usage on a team that does not need him.

case.label: What the old clause measured
case.body: The 18 September row said six or more targets against Detroit makes him a claim. He drew six, so the clause fired and the row was carried. Six targets on a 60% route share is a worse fact than six targets alone, and the clause never asked about routes. Same mistake as the Brian Thomas clause, on the same day.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Shakir crossing 75% of Buffalo's routes. Not a target count — that is what got this wrong twice.
